verdict.rationale: Jitsu supports several background automations that run without ongoing user intervention: Functions that filter/transform/enrich data automatically before delivery, Connector Syncs that run as scheduled Kubernetes CronJobs, dead-letter reprocessing workers, and automated failure/recovery alerts via Slack/Email. These are genuinely autonomous, always-on pipeline behaviors once configured, and the MCP server even lets an AI agent set them up itself. However, this is data-pipeline automation (transform, sync, alert) rather than general-purpose agentic workflow automation, and there's no evidence of conditional/triggered multi-step 'autonomous agent' workflows beyond data processing. Missing for 10: evidence of flexible/generalized scheduling or trigger-based workflow automation beyond data functions/syncs, and independent (non-vendor) confirmation that these automations run reliably unattended.
